chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Ismail al-Madainy, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from a man who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) ordered meat, and it became cold. Then it was brought to him later, so he said: 'Praise is to Allah, the One who made me desire it.' Then he said: 'The blessing in health is superior to the blessing upon ability (to acquire/eat).'
ai.seo_question: What is the etiquette of praising Allah before eating according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) illustrates the etiquette of eating by praising Allah for the desire to eat even when the food had cooled down, highlighting that the blessing of physical health and capacity is superior to the mere ability to obtain or consume food. This narration, found in al-Kafi, underscores the Shia emphasis on gratitude (shukr) for the internal faculties of the body rather than just external provisions. It serves as a practical reminder to recognize the 'ni'mah' (blessing) of well-being as the prerequisite for enjoying any worldly comfort.

en.hubeali: A number of our companion, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from Ismail Al Madainy, from Abdullah Bin Bukeyr, from a man who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> ordered with the meat, but it got cold. Then they came with it from afterwards. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The Praise is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Whom Made me desire it’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The Bounty during the good health is better than the Bounty upon the measured (constraint)’.
en.sarwar: 24. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ya‘qub ibn Yazid from ’Isma‘il al-Mada’iniy from ‘Abd Allah ibn Bukayr from a man who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, commanded to bring meat but it became cold and later it was brought. He (the Imam) said, ‘All praise belongs to Allah who made me to have the appetite for it.’ He (the Imam) then said, ‘Bounty in good health is better than the bounty with constraints.”’
